verification.note: Read from the product having one load, which its group 1 controls, as on other one-load products.

steps.text: Turn on your lamp and plug its power cord into the bottom of the dimmer module.
Plug the dimmer module into an unswitched wall outlet.

notes: Leave the lamp's own switch on; if it is off, the module can't control the lamp.
Only connect lamps with dimmable bulbs.

verification.note: Read from the Dimmer Plug 2457D2 Owner's Manual; no 2457D2X document was found.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button to enter linking mode.

notes: Linking is directional: the first device put into linking mode becomes the controller and the second the responder. The module leaves linking mode once a link is made or after four minutes without one.

As a responder: on the controller, press and hold the SET button (on a multi-button controller, tap the button first) until it beeps; make sure the module is on, then press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps.
To have two devices control each other, cross-link them: link once in each direction.
When using the Hub or another central controller, let it manage links instead of linking manually.

verification.note: When adding the module to the Hub, the Dimmer Plug 2457D2 Owner's Manual says to hold the SET button until the module double-beeps; the Dimmer Plug 2457D2 Quick Start Guide says until it beeps. The catalog's linking step gives no beep count.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button to enter linking mode.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder; the device makes no link back to the Hub, since this profile lists no group it controls.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button to enter linking mode.
Tap the SET button to move to multi-linking mode.
Press and hold the SET button on each responder until it double-beeps.
Tap the SET button to finish.

notes: The module stays in multi-linking mode for 4 minutes or until its SET button is tapped.

verification.note: Read from the Dimmer Plug 2457D2 Owner's Manual's local programming flowchart (press and hold to move right, tap to move down) and the multi-linking description; it has no step-by-step multi-linking procedure for the module itself.

steps.text: With the controller in unlinking mode, press and hold the SET button until the module double-beeps.

notes: Put the controller in unlinking mode first: press and hold its SET button until it beeps (on a multi-button controller, tap the button first), then press and hold it again until it beeps.
In its own unlinking mode the module leaves the mode once a link is removed or after four minutes.

verification.note: Read from the Dimmer Plug 2457D2 Owner's Manual; no 2457D2X document was found.

steps.text: Unplug the dimmer module from its outlet.
Press and hold the SET button while plugging the module back in.
Keep holding the SET button until the module stops beeping.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: Double beep when the reset is complete

verification.note: Read from the Dimmer Plug 2457D2 Owner's Manual; no 2457D2X document was found.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a responder.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: Inferred: seen on three i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48, I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245, these steps should remove the modem's group 0 link with no SET button press: the modem starts ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF while the device is sent Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09). This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

Inferred: seen on an i2CS device (I/O Module 2450 firmware 0x41) linked to a Hub 2245: unlinking by the modem's own records left the device's records for the Hub's other groups, and an i2CS device answers a device that's in its ALL-Link database. So a device that still answers the Hub after removal may hold other records for it; a factory reset, as this profile's reset steps give it, clears them. This applies to the firmware versions this profile's engines give as i2CS.

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.
